title: React Working Flow: From Components to UI
description: Understand how React works from start to finish — components, JSX, props, state, events, rendering, the Virtual DOM, re-renders, hooks, and how React updates the browser UI.

title: Object Oriented Programming
description: Master OOP for LLD: classes, objects, responsibilities, encapsulation, abstraction, inheritance, polymorphism, interfaces, abstract classes, and object relationships such as association, aggregation, composition, and dependency. Build strong object-thinking skills and choose composition vs inheritance effectively.

title: DSA Pattern Recognition Cheat Sheet
description: A quick-reference guide covering 25 recurring DSA patterns, their trigger clues, and recognition techniques to help you identify the right pattern before writing code.

title: Computer Networks Part 1: From Bits to NAT
description: Build a strong mental model of networking from layers, bits, signals, and NICs to frames, MAC addresses, switches, IP addressing, routers, ARP, IPv4, private/public IPs, and NAT.

title: Computer Networks Part 2: Transport Layer, Ports & Sockets
description: Understand how networking moves from host-to-host delivery to application-level communication through ports, TCP and UDP, ephemeral ports, 4-tuples, sockets, listening connections, and NAT port mapping.

title: Computer Networks Part 3: TCP Reliability & Congestion Control
description: Dive into TCP internals including the 3-way handshake, sequence numbers, ACKs, retransmission, out-of-order data, sliding windows, flow control, congestion control, Slow Start, connection termination, FIN, RST, and TIME_WAIT.

title: Computer Networks Part 4: DNS, HTTP, HTTPS & CDN
description: Understand how applications communicate over the network through DNS resolution, HTTP requests and responses, HTTPS with TLS and certificates, HTTP caching, and CDNs that deliver content closer to users.

title: Computer Networks Part 5: Proxies, Architecture & Network Security
description: Complete the SDE-1 networking picture with CDNs, forward and reverse proxies, load balancers, VPNs, API gateways, 3-tier architecture, monoliths vs microservices, CORS, network security, common attacks, MTU, PMTUD, and end-to-end request flows.

title: System Design Fundamentals & Networking
description: Learn core system design concepts including scalability, availability, reliability, performance, fault tolerance, and trade-offs. Understand DNS, TCP/UDP, HTTP/HTTPS, TLS, REST, authentication, sessions, JWT, load balancers, and databases. Practice client-server architecture, request flows, bottleneck identification, and scaling real-world systems.
